scenes.anchor_text: It was a Tuesday, and the calendar had just ticked over to January 3rd. A terrible winter storm had descended on North America, and half the country was buried in snow and ice. In Seattle we didn’t have too much snow that night. But it was well below zero, which was unusually cold, even for January.
scenes.scene_description: A wide establishing shot of Seattle during an unusually cold January night, with a light dusting of snow and a heavy overcast sky. The city lights are muted and hazy.

scenes.anchor_text:
Me, I didn’t have a choice. Like I said, it was below freezing. I was outside. And I was wearing boxers, a leather jacket, and a pair of pink Crocs sandals that barely fit me.

I was also holding a crying, scratching, squirming, and spitting cat named Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk.

scenes.anchor_text: So when I woke up at about two A.M., having been startled awake by a dream, I decided I needed a smoke. I pulled out my pack, cracked the window, and I lit a cigarette.
scenes.scene_description: A dimly lit bedroom with a man sitting on the edge of the bed smoking a cigarette, with a cracked window showing a snowy night outside.

scenes.anchor_text: She jumped up on my shoulder, and she leaped out the second-story window onto the tree outside my apartment. Just like that. I’d had that window open dozens of times over the past year, and she’d never even given the window a second glance.
scenes.scene_description: A tortoiseshell Persian cat leaps from a second-story window onto a snow-covered tree branch outside.

scenes.anchor_text: She scampered down the tree, sniffed at the sidewalk a few times, and then promptly realized it was cold as fuck. Her adventure over as quickly as it began, she rushed back up the tree and stared at me over the five feet from the window to the branch.
scenes.scene_description: The Persian cat perched on a tree branch, staring back at the open window with a disgruntled expression. Snow covers the ground.

scenes.anchor_text: I rushed down the stairs, and I jumped outside, rushing to the tree that sat between the sidewalk and the building. I immediately regretted not taking the time to put proper clothes on. The cold, windy air sunk its claws into my legs and feet.
scenes.scene_description: A man in boxers and Crocs rushes outside towards a tree, the cold winter air visibly biting at his exposed skin.

scenes.anchor_text: The window on the first-floor apartment slid open. “What in god’s name is going on out here?” Mrs. Parsons called, sticking her head out the window. The old woman had her head wrapped in a some sort of towel, making her look like a swami.
scenes.scene_description: An old woman with her head wrapped in a towel peers out of a first-floor window, looking annoyed at the commotion outside.

scenes.anchor_text: The building smashed down to the ground. I watched it happen. The seven-story apartment building was there one moment, and then it was gone. But it hadn’t disappeared. I was looking right at Mrs. Parsons when it went down.
scenes.scene_description: The moment a seven-story apartment building is instantaneously crushed, viewed from the street level. The sky darkens abruptly.

scenes.anchor_text: Everything was gone except the trees and the bicycles in the bike racks, and Marjory Williams’s moped that was still booted by parking enforcement.

scenes.anchor_text: I looked around, the freezing weather momentarily forgotten. In the dark, overcast night, I could barely see anything. In the distance—a distance I could now see thanks to the lack of buildings—a fire burned.
scenes.scene_description: A man stands amidst the rubble, looking around at the changed landscape. In the distance, a fire burns.

scenes.anchor_text:
All that remained of my building was a rectangle of churned dirt and rocks.

And then I saw it, right near my feet.

It was Mrs. Parson’s head. In the dark, it was hard to discern. But I immediately knew what it was.
scenes.scene_description: A close-up on the ground revealing a severed head amidst the rubble and churned earth. The remains of the crushed building are visible in the background.

scenes.anchor_text: The voice was like a physical thing. A spike in my brain, scratching me. It wasn’t speaking English. But I understood the words. As the person spoke, the text also appeared floating in front of me.
scenes.scene_description: Floating, alien text appears in the air in front of a bewildered man, bathed in an eerie light. The environment is dark and destroyed.

scenes.anchor_text: Less than a hundred feet to my left, right in the middle of what had once been a thrift store, a spotlight burst into the air. I saw an additional spotlight appear about a mile away. I turned, and I saw a few more littered throughout the city.
